correctness.rationale: The area inequalities are equivalent to 0≤p_i<i and nondecreasing p_i; these parent-index conditions give a rooted tree whose children's blocks, traversed by queue in increasing parent order, yield exactly labels 0,…,n. Conversely breadth-first labelling yields those conditions and hence the unique area sequence. The earlier nonneighbors of i are exactly 1,…,p_i, so the maximum independent size ending at i is 1+max_{0≤j≤p_i} b_j, with b_0=0. The nested prefixes make b_i nondecreasing, giving b_i=1+b_{p_i} and equality with the breadth-first depth. The greedy partition starting each next block at the first vertex t with p_t≥ the previous start indeed has clique blocks; its starts form an independent set, giving a matching certificate of optimality without a connectedness assumption. The bounded-height plane-tree recurrence H_h=1/(1−zH_{h−1}), H_0=1, gives the stated continuants. For m=1,2,3, the positive-degree coefficients follow by recurrence/partial fractions, with the third denominator (1−z)(1−3z) and the second the odd Fibonacci recurrence. n=0 is used only as the height-zero generating-function seed. The height claim concerns the contour of the new tree, not the original area-sequence path or an unlabeled graph class. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: There is a genuine alternate formulation: p_i is the horizontal coordinate of north step i in the original path. From diagonal contact b, the next bounce contact's coordinate is max{i:p_i≤b}. This is the update both for the last label at the next breadth-first depth (starting with root label 0) and for the end of the next greedy clique block (starting at b+1). Thus the original graph statistic is the number of positive bounce parts, not the weighted bounce sum or the height of the original path. The known bounce composition supplies the path statistic but no inspected source gives the graph interpretation and its resulting m-Abelian count.

originality.rationale: No credit is assigned to the Catalan/plane-tree bijection in isolation, the bounded-height enumerator, or the m=1 graph count. residual_risks: Historical proper-interval graph orderings and Catalan bounce/level encodings admit several synonyms.
